I am 60 this year. I have farmed these 7.5 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I never went to school. My father taught me everything, and I learned the rest by watching my neighbors and doing it myself. I do not trust strangers who come with notebooks — I only trust what I see work on someone else's field.

The wheat is already in the ground. I planted 5 mu last October with improved seed I bought from the dealer in town. Right now it is greening up. At sowing I put one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer — the kind with the three numbers on it — into the soil. When the wheat wakes up in spring I will spread half a bag of urea. At jointing stage, another half bag. That is one full bag of urea per mu for the year. I always irrigate three times: once before winter to keep it from freezing dry, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice — once for aphids, once for the rust. I rotary-till before I sow. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, so 450 kg. If the weather is like last year, I will get the same.

After we harvest the wheat in June, I plant 5 mu of hybrid maize on that same land. I buy new hybrid seed every year — everyone does, you cannot save your own maize seed. I do not till much for maize, just plant right into the wheat stubble. I put one 50-jin bag of compound in the row at planting. Then when the plants are knee-high I top-dress with one big bag of urea. I irrigate twice if the rains are thin. Two sprays — one for armyworm, one for the ear rot. I usually get about 1,000 jin per mu, so 500 kg.

My cotton is 2.5 mu. Cotton is hard work, and with just my wife and me, I cannot handle more. I plough deep in spring to break up the soil. I plant an improved variety — not the old local cotton my grandfather grew, but not those fancy expensive hybrid seeds either. I put one 100-jin bag of compound as base, then two top-dressings of urea — half a bag at flowering, half a bag when the bolls are setting. Cotton needs more potash, so I make sure the compound bag has that third number. I irrigate four times: at planting, at flowering, at boll setting, and when the bolls are opening. Five pesticide sprays — the bollworm never sleeps, and if you miss one spray you lose the crop. Last year I got about 520 jin of seed cotton per mu, so 260 kg. I expect the same.

Fertilizer is expensive now. Every bag is real money out of my pocket. But I would rather put a little too much than risk losing yield. A bad harvest at my age is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I do what I did last year. I watch Old Wang across the road. If he puts more urea on his wheat, I think about it. If he cuts back, I wonder why. Change is dangerous when you have only this land to live on.
